exposure: Date fruit consumption (seven dates per day from 35 weeks onwards)
outcome: Delivery outcomes (spontaneous vaginal delivery, instrumental delivery, caesarean section)
Bishop score at onset of labour
cohort: 140 nulliparous pregnant women were randomized into experimental and control groups to assess the effect of date fruit consumption.
finding: Date fruit consumption in later pregnancy was associated with an improved Bishop score at the onset of labour, a shorter duration of labour, a lesser need for induction and augmentation of labour, and more spontaneous vaginal deliveries.
mod_finding: Date fruit consumption led to more spontaneous vaginal deliveries and fewer instrumental or caesarean section deliveries.
